idiom_name: ActiveRecord belongs_to/has_many over the author_id column
implementation_notes: ActiveRecord derives the mapping from association macros: belongs_to :author on Book manages the author_id column, has_many :books on Author reads the same column, and belongs_to validates presence of the target by default. The generated methods (association=, build_association, association_changed?) replace the mapper's resolve and write steps, while includes(:author) versus a lazy read decides when the row is fetched. A hand-written mapper (find_by_sql plus explicit id handling) is justified for reporting queries or legacy tables that do not follow the *_id convention.
code_sketch:
class Book < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :author, optional: false     # stores author_id
end

class Author < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :books, dependent: :destroy
end
# migration: t.belongs_to :author, foreign_key: true -> author_id + real FK
pitfalls: belongs_to's presence validation is not a database foreign key: without foreign_key: true in the migration, any other writer can orphan rows.
Iterating books and calling book.author queries per row unless includes/preload is used, and dependent: :destroy loads the whole child collection before deleting it.
accepts_nested_attributes_for plus belongs_to means a child can be reassigned by id straight from request parameters - check ownership, not just existence.
